body_summary: RD-14 reframed: confirm the created account cannot perform any admin action despite the role:'admin' injection attempt
ai_reasoning: RD-14 only checked the JWT's role claim. This extension goes one step further and actually calls an admin-gated action (POST /api/admin/coupons from the main homework) with the resulting token, to prove the ignored field has no real security consequence here -- unlike API3's actual privilege-escalation bug, which needed no injection at all.
audit_notes: Confirmed: the RD-14 account's token, used against POST /api/admin/coupons, still succeeds with 200 -- but that's because of API3's SEPARATE missing-role-check bug (already reported), not because of this registration's role-injection attempt (which was correctly ignored). Important distinction documented: registration's mass-assignment defense is real and independent of API3's unrelated access-control bug.

audit_notes: Confirmed: coupons.code is declared UNIQUE in the schema and enforced (PC-04 in the main homework got a 500 on a duplicate); users.email has no such constraint anywhere and duplicates are silently accepted (RD-09). Same codebase, inconsistent data-integrity discipline between two tables -- worth flagging as a general code-quality observation, not just a single-endpoint bug.

audit_notes: Confirmed: 200, account created despite every field being simultaneously hostile. The SQLi is neutralized by parameterization (as RD-10 already showed), but the duplicate-email and empty-password gaps both still apply independently -- no combined defense emerges from the individual (partial) protections.
